Thanks for letting me know. Not sure why this wasn't done automatically by Firefox's `mach bootstrap`. I will go ahead and add it to the Dockerfile.

Unfortunately Firefox's build process can be unpredictable for different OS targets. I hope it didn't cause you too much trouble.

> Why it is trying to download go again?

Go tries to download its toolchains on the spot when building. I was able to fix the `toolchain not found` issues in Docker after changing `go 1.23` to `go 1.23.0` in go.mod.

### Root issue

In the original version of Juggler, an internal tree of all frames is kept as they are created/destroyed on the page. Playwright's FrameLocator uses this frame tree to find iframes when frame_locator is called.

However, when Juggler collects frames for its internal FrameTree frame, it creates an execution context within each frame to send input events. Some WAFs are able to detect this. I had no choice but to strip it from Juggler, which is why `.click()` fails.

### Solution

For now, you should be able to evaluate JavaScript on the page to access iframes as you would in a normal browser.

I will be working on a fix to restore FrameLocator functionality through an alternative approach to creating the frame tree.

The detection of proxies isn't done at the browser level, it's done at the network level. Unfortunately there isn't anything that can be done in Camoufox that can fix it, besides switching to a provider that doesn't cause flags.

The User Agent detection works by checking for JS behavior that is specific to Firefox 130, and comparing it to the claimed userAgent (in this case 125). In my testing, I've only seen this specific to BrowserScan.net, and it doesn't seem to be used by WAFs in production at the moment (maybe in the future). 

Because having a broad range of User Agents is helpful in avoiding detection for most other websites, I've decided against locking the userAgent version in order to get around this edge case. In the future, I do plan on locking it.

Hello, these values are expected. Here's an explanation:

- In Camoufox, WebGL is disabled.  `d616acaa8a5b82727e84b66e71209f5d841f07b0` is BrowserScan's default hash value for when there is no WebGL detected, and `412238758ac572ee55fd2705260e649b6912ad1e` is the default Canvas fingerprint for Firefox 130+ without WebGL. This is expected.
- Audio fingerprint rotation has not been implemented into Camoufox just yet, but Camoufox will hide your device labels. `d970cc255a6553bdb52a03310340dee87c6cf7c1` is BrowserScan's default audio fingerprint when no audio devices labels are detected. This is the same across all versions of Firefox, and isn't anything specific to Camoufox.
- Font fingerprinting in BrowserScan is based off the names of your installed font families. By default, Camoufox uses the standard set of fonts pulled from Windows 11 22H2, macOS Sonma, and the default Linux fonts used in the TOR browser. It's very unlikely that this set would be used to fingerprinting since it's as if the user is using a fresh install of the OS without any fonts installed. However, if you'd like to add additional fonts to rotate through, you can randomly passed the names of font families installed on your system into the `fonts` parameter in the Python library.

Hello, thanks for the suggestions! Here's a couple notes:

> Random starting point and random end point for clicking the elements

I had this idea as well, but I held off on it because of the way Playwright handles clicking elements. On the browser side, I only receive the coordinates of where to click, not the element to click itself. The Playwright client library determines the mouse coordinates on it's own without telling the browser which element it's clicking. In other words, I would need to patch the Playwright client library itself, which is something I want to avoid to keep support for other languages with Playwright/remotely accessing Camoufox from the official Playwright library.

A workaround for this could be to lie about the element's width/height and position to fool Playwright into clicking at a random point besides the center, but this will require more testing to see if it breaks anything else.

> Auto click for cloudflare turnstile

I could possibly add a `autoclick` property for automatically clicking elements as they appear.

> Random sleeps while key press down and up

I'm planning on adding this soon, but I was wondering how I wanted to implement it. I think I'll add a `humanize:wpm` and `humanize:wpm:sd` to set a custom typing WPM/standard deviation.

> Adding noise to canvas and webgl fingerprinting

This is actually implemented into Firefox itself. You can enable Canvas randomization and WebGL fingerprint protection like this:

```python
with Camoufox(

I looked into how Pixelscan works, here are some notes:
- Pixelscan raises the "Automation framework detected" flag with the width and height of the generated screen fingerprint is 1280x720. Typically, anti-bots only ever flag if the inner window viewport is 1280x720. This seems aggressive, and likely won't ever be used in a production WAF. However, when a new fingerprint generator library is created for Camoufox (which will be coming soon), I will consider omitting anything with a standard 1280x720 resolution.
- The "Very likely you are masking your fingerprint flag" flag is caused by the failing voices, media device, and WebGL tests. Voice injection has been added to Camoufox recently, and media device injection will be added soon. However, these properties won't be automatically generated and populated until the new fingerprint generator is ready. Additionally, a custom Vulkan driver  is currently being worked on to help with WebGL/Canvas fp injection.

Hello,

- Manually passing in BrowserForge fingerprints is deprecated (this will typically raise a warning when `i_know_what_im_doing` is disabled). This can cause some unexpected inconsistencies.
    - Camoufox doesn't use all of BrowserForge's fingerprint data. If you'd like to set the WebGL renderer and vendor, this can be done through the config properties [here](https://camoufox.com/fingerprint/webgl/#properties). However, your true GPU can still be detected through your WebGL parameters, shader percisions, and context attributes (CreepJS detects this). Because of this, WebGL isn't enabled by default in Camoufox and isn't recommended to use.
- Setting the screen width and height doesn't set the screen's avaliable width and height, which can cause mismatch leaks. The Python library typically will handle this on its own. Although, if you'd like to see a full set of the config sent to Camoufox to avoid mismatches, you can enable `debug=True`.

> Canvas, WebGL report and Audio fingerprint has same values on 1 machine with different browsers, according to browserscan.net

Heres an explanation:

- In Camoufox, WebGL is disabled (as for now). The value you are seeing is BrowserScan's default hash value for when there is no WebGL detected.
- Canvas fingerprint rotation is still WIP ([see here for updates](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/discussions/41)). Camoufox does not use the standard Canvas fingerprint rotation as it can be detected. Additionally, since WebGL is disabled, BrowserScan does not record the 3D rendering fingerprint either, resulting in a less unique value.
- Audio signal fingerprint rotation has not been implemented into Camoufox yet either. However, you can manually override AudioContext data [here](https://camoufox.com/fingerprint/audiocontext/).
- Font fingerprinting in BrowserScan is based off the names of your installed font families. By default, Camoufox uses the standard set of fonts pulled from Windows 11 22H2, macOS Sonma, and the default Linux fonts used in the TOR browser. It's very unlikely that this set would be used to fingerprinting since it's as if the user is using a fresh install of the OS without any fonts installed. However, if you'd like to add additional fonts to rotate through, you can randomly pass the names of font families installed on your system into the fonts parameter in the Python library.

The fingerprint injection TODO list is available [here](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/discussions/40).

Hello,

1. `dom.event.clipboardevents.enabled = false`
You are right, this line should be removed. I believe I forgot to remove it from the BetterFox config. 😅 

2. `dom.ipc.processCount = 1`
Playwright's [original preference](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/browser_patches/firefox/preferences/playwright.cfg#L37) uses infinite processes, and this caused a heavy CPU overhead load (I left a comment [here](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/main/settings/camoufox.cfg#L461) about it). When I set this, I had only planned for Camoufox to be optimized for 1 context and 1 tab. However, I can see the value in disabling this for a performance boost. I will revert it back to the original Playwright preference.

3. `privacy.resistFingerprinting = false`
This is intentionally disabled, and enabling this can hurt Camoufox's stealth. RFP mimics how TOR makes all users look the same by standardizing [these values](https://wiki.mozilla.org/Security/Fingerprinting) and blocking access to certain browser APIs. Enabling this can be easily detected by websites and raises suspicions from Creepjs, Cloudflare, etc. Camoufox's goal is to inject it's own believable fingerprint data into these APIs rather than blocking them off completely or setting them to a standard value.

I figured out that reason this issue doesn't happen when using the route solution is because headers aren't being passed to `route.fulfill`:

```python
async def handle_route(route):
    response = await route.fetch()
    await route.fulfill(
        body=await response.body(),
        headers=response.headers,  # Missing in example
        status=response.status
    )
```

Specifically, the reason Turnstile can be clicked is because the `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` (or COOP) header is being removed. Seems like Playwright's click function does not support the latest security changes in FF133+.

A workaround for this could be to use this preference which disables COOP from being handled:

```python
firefox_user_prefs={
    'browser.tabs.remote.useCrossOriginOpenerPolicy': False,
}
```

However, this could potentially be detected by anti-bots, though I haven't seen this used in a production environment (all major anti-bot providers & Camoufox testing sites still pass with it disabled). I will consider adding a COOP toggle in the Python library until Playwright bumps to FF133+ 👍

Hello, thanks for the PR. Sorry I didn't have a chance to fully test it! I was hesitant to add it since many compatibility and leak issues can be caused by the python library running on older Camoufox versions, since new parameters are added into the browser and in the Playwright library all the time. It's typically better to always use the latest beta, despite there sometimes being some regressions.

I am considering an alternative, to make a user "Camoufox Manager" UI that allows looking up and fetching multiple Camoufox versions and refactoring the library to handle version compatibility differences better. I'm also thinking of separating the giant fonts folder into it's own repository to pull from, since it typically stays the same between versions and isn't worth redownloading hundreds of megabytes each update. I plan on beginning this all in the upcoming weeks/months once my classes are more out of my way. :+1:

I have figured this one out, @iloveitaly. It has to do with the quality of the MaxMind GeoIP data for certain IPs. MaxMind is the database that Camoufox uses to pull geolocation data for IPs. You can check https://www.maxmind.com/en/geoip-demo for a given IP address, to see what it will give you. For some proxy IPs, GeoIP just returns the center of the continental US, in Kansas. See below example below for the IP address you sent above: This generic location also often gives me bad languages, which additionally lowers my % on BrowserScan (I haven't looked into how default language is setup in Camoufox code...) There are two ways around this: 1. For static IPs, you can set geoip=False and instead set a custom config for where your static IP is. For example, if your static IP is in NYC, you can set the following ``` geoip=False, #optional, as default is false proxy={ 'server':, 'username':, 'password': } config={ 'timezone':'America/New_York', 'geolocation:latitude':40.7130 'geolocation:longitude':-74.006 'locale:language':'en', 'locale:region':'US', 'locale:script':'Latn', 'webrtc:ipv4': } ``` optionally, you can instead leave out the 'webrtc:ipv4' from the config, and set `block_webrtc=True` 2. For rotating IPs, I've found that Residential Proxies tend to have better results from MaxMind, so maybe those will work out of the box. If not, some proxy providers allow you to restrict locations to certain states or cities. If you set your rotating proxy to California, say, you could set the lat/lon to San Francisco, and block_webrtc=true. Then timezones will match. Without any of the above, if MaxMind doesn't have accurate data for your IP, you'll sometimes get lucky, and your proxy geolocation will be the same timezone as your actual proxy. Well I found the answer myself. For those interested you need to activate: `main_world_eval=True`
in the Camoufox constructor same place where you configure `headless`.
 ```
async with AsyncCamoufox(
        headless=i_bHeadless,
        os=chosen_os,
        screen=Screen(max_width=i_iWidth, max_height=i_iHeight),
        locale="en-US",
        main_world_eval=True
    ) as browser:
        yield browser
```
Then you can access with the suffix `mw: ` in the function `.evaluate()` the global variable for example: 
```
varName = "flashvars"
await page.evaluate(f"mw:window.{varName}") # await because i use async
```
or
```
varName = "flashvars"
await page.evaluate(f'mw:window["{varName}"]') # await because i use async
```

The global Variable `varName` needs to be the string to the original `var flashvars = { titleName: "", url: "" etc };` you wish to access.
If you need like in my case more than one line. Then you need to F-String the Function like this:

```
varName = "flashvars"
links = await page.evaluate(f"""    # await because i use async
        mw:() => {{
             let value = false;
             if(typeof window["{varName}"] !== 'undefined'){{
                 value = true;
             }}
             return value;
          }}
          """)
```
ps: Important as well if you use F-String you need to embedd every {{ }} double.

This is how I managed to directly access global variables. Hopefully in the near future there will be an easier method for this.

Here is a temporary fix. To get your Dockerfiles to build, or use Camoufox normally for the time being.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Download browserforge data files from a compatible version.
This ensures compatibility with Camoufox v135.0.1-beta.24
"""

import os
import sys
import shutil
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

# Use v2.1.66 for compatibility with older browserforge API
FINGERPRINT_SUITE_VERSION = "v2.1.66"

def download_file(url, destination):
    """Download a file from URL to destination."""
    print(f"Downloading: {url}")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response:
            with open(destination, 'wb') as out_file:
                shutil.copyfileobj(response, out_file)
        print(f"Downloaded: {destination}")
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error downloading {url}: {e}")
        return False

def extract_zip(zip_path, extract_to):
    """Extract a zip file."""
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as zip_ref:
            zip_ref.extractall(extract_to)
        print(f"Extracted: {zip_path}")
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error extracting {zip_path}: {e}")
        return False

def find_browserforge_path():
    """Find the browserforge installation path."""
    try:
        import browserforge

        # Try to get the file path
        if hasattr(browserforge, '__file__') and browserforge.__file__:
            return Path(browserforge.__file__).parent

        # If __file__ is None, try to find it in site-packages
        import site
        import importlib.util

        # Try to find the module spec
        spec = importlib.util.find_spec('browserforge')
        if spec and spec.submodule_search_locations:
            for location in spec.submodule_search_locations:
                if location and os.path.exists(location):
                    return Path(location)

        # Fall back to searching site-packages
        for site_dir in site.getsitepackages():
            potential_path = Path(site_dir) / 'browserforge'
            if potential_path.exists():
                return potential_path

        # Also check user site-packages
        user_site = site.getusersitepackages()
        if user_site:
            potential_path = Path(user_site) / 'browserforge'
            if potential_path.exists():
                return potential_path

        return None

    except ImportError:
        return None

def main():
    # Find browserforge installation path
    bf_path = find_browserforge_path()

    if not bf_path:
        print("Error: browserforge not installed or cannot find installation path.")
        print("Please install browserforge first: pip install browserforge==1.1.0")
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"Found browserforge at: {bf_path}")

    # Create data directories
    headers_data_dir = bf_path / "headers" / "data"
    fingerprints_data_dir = bf_path / "fingerprints" / "data"

    # Clean existing data directories if they exist
    print("Cleaning existing data files...")
    if headers_data_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(headers_data_dir)
        print(f"Removed existing headers data directory: {headers_data_dir}")

    if fingerprints_data_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(fingerprints_data_dir)
        print(f"Removed existing fingerprints data directory: {fingerprints_data_dir}")

    # Recreate the directories
    headers_data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fingerprints_data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Define files to download
    base_url = f"https://github.com/apify/fingerprint-suite/raw/{FINGERPRINT_SUITE_VERSION}"

    downloads = [
        # Headers data files
        (
            f"{base_url}/packages/header-generator/src/data_files/browser-helper-file.json",
            headers_data_dir / "browser-helper-file.json"
        ),
        (
            f"{base_url}/packages/header-generator/src/data_files/header-network-definition.zip",
            headers_data_dir / "header-network.zip"
        ),
        (
            f"{base_url}/packages/header-generator/src/data_files/headers-order.json",
            headers_data_dir / "headers-order.json"
        ),
        (
            f"{base_url}/packages/header-generator/src/data_files/input-network-definition.zip",
            headers_data_dir / "input-network.zip"
        ),
        # Fingerprints data files
        (
            f"{base_url}/packages/fingerprint-generator/src/data_files/fingerprint-network-definition.zip",
            fingerprints_data_dir / "fingerprint-network.zip"
        ),
    ]

    # Download all files
    success = True
    for url, destination in downloads:
        if not download_file(url, destination):
            success = False
            break

    if not success:
        print("Failed to download all required files.")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Extract zip files
    zip_files = [
        headers_data_dir / "header-network.zip",
        headers_data_dir / "input-network.zip",
        fingerprints_data_dir / "fingerprint-network.zip"
    ]

    for zip_file in zip_files:
        if zip_file.exists():
            extract_to = zip_file.parent
            if not extract_zip(zip_file, extract_to):
                print(f"Warning: Failed to extract {zip_file}")

    print(f"Successfully downloaded browserforge data files from {FINGERPRINT_SUITE_VERSION}")

    # Verify critical files exist
    critical_files = [
        headers_data_dir / "browser-helper-file.json",
        headers_data_dir / "headers-order.json",
        fingerprints_data_dir / "fingerprint-network.zip"
    ]

    for file in critical_files:
        if not file.exists():
            print(f"Error: Critical file missing: {file}")
            sys.exit(1)

    print("All critical files verified.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

def process_response_for_recaptcha(response_text, grid_size=(3,3)):

[True, True, False, False, True, False, False, False, False]

solution = [False] * total_cells
try:
# Try to extract numbers from the response

numbers = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r'\d+', response_text)]
for num in numbers:
if 1 <= num <= total_cells:
solution[num - 1] = True
return solution
except Exception as e:
print(f"[!] Error processing response: {e}")
return solution

**Fix for script hanging when window is minimized/backgrounded**

I encountered the same issue where the script execution hangs or throttles significantly when the browser window is minimized, occluded, or switched to the background.

This is caused by Firefox's Window Occlusion Tracking and Background Throttling mechanisms (designed to save resources).

I managed to fix this by disabling the relevant flags via firefox_user_prefs. Here is the configuration that works for me:

Python

## Acknowledgement & Appreciation

First and foremost, I want to express my sincere gratitude to the **CloverLabsAI team** for picking up the torch and maintaining this project. 

As many of us in the community know, the original author (`daijro`) has been dealing with health issues since March, leaving the project in limbo. Seeing your work on the **v146 update**—especially the complex migration from JSM to ESM—is incredibly encouraging. You are literally saving this tool for the community. Thank you!

---

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

**Context:**
We are utilizing the new `camoufox-beta` (v146) for an automation workflow that requires strict session persistence. We use `persistent_context=True` with a specified `user_data_dir`.

**The Problem:**
While `persistent_context` successfully retains storage states (Cookies, LocalStorage), **hardware fingerprint attributes and noise seeds are randomly regenerated on every launch**.

Specifically:
1.  **Fingerprint ID Drift:** The Canvas/WebGL noise seeds change on restart. Even with the same cookies, the "VisitorID" (generated by FingerprintJS) changes because the underlying rendering output shifts.
2.  **Hardware Mismatch:** `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` drifts (e.g., changes from 16 -> 12), and GPU Renderer strings vary randomly.

**Current Limitation:**
Using `user_data_dir` **does not persist** these hardware randomization seeds. This leads to a scenario where a logged-in user (persisted cookies) suddenly appears with a different CPU and Graphics Card (randomized hardware), triggering "Session Hijacking" or high-risk flags in anti-fraud systems.

## Describe the solution you'd like

We request a mechanism to **persist the randomization seeds** and hardware configuration within the `user_data_dir` (or via a config object).

**Expected Behavior:**
When launching with `persistent_context=True` and pointing to an existing `user_data_dir`:
1.  Camoufox should read the previously generated **Canvas/WebGL/Audio noise seeds** from the profile, ensuring the exact same "Fingerprint ID" is generated.
2.  Hardware attributes (Concurrency, GPU Vendor) used in the previous session should be restored.

**Goal:**
A "Clone-able" or "Freezable" browser environment where the device fingerprint remains static across reboots.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

1.  **JS Injection:** Using `add_init_script` to mock values. 
    * *Cons:* Fails in **Web Workers** (critical for advanced detection) and cannot perfectly replicate Canvas noise patterns.
2.  **Keep-Alive:** Never closing the browser. 
    * *Cons:* Not scalable for resource management.

## Additional context

- **Impact:** Critical for long-term account management.
- **Camoufox Version:** v146-beta.25
- **OS:** Linux (Ubuntu) / Windows

[Windows/Cross-Compile] Fixes for pid_t/headers, Build Script Logic & Feature Request: Persistent Fingerprints

I have been working on cross-compiling the Windows version of Camoufox and encountered several blocking issues related to POSIX type definitions, missing headers, and the patch application logic in scripts/patch.py.

Below is a summary of the errors I faced and the solutions I implemented to successfully build the project. Additionally, I have a feature request regarding Fingerprint Persistence at the end of this report.

1. Compilation & Code Fixes
A. Missing pid_t Definition (Windows)
Error: error: unknown type name 'pid_t' Cause: pid_t is a POSIX type and is not defined by default in the Windows cross-compile environment (MinGW/MSVC), yet it is used in WebRTC headers included by Juggler. Fix: Added a conditional typedef in juggler/screencast/HeadlessWindowCapturer.h and juggler/screencast/nsScreencastService.cpp.

C++

#if defined(XP_WIN) || defined(_WIN32) || defined(__MINGW32__)
#ifndef _PID_T_DEFINED
#define _PID_T_DEFINED
typedef int pid_t;
#endif
#endif
B. Incomplete Type DrawTarget
Error: error: member access into incomplete type 'mozilla::gfx::DrawTarget' Fix: Added #include "mozilla/gfx/2D.h" to widget/headless/HeadlessCompositorWidget.cpp to ensure the type is fully defined.

C. Missing scoped_refptr.h for Playwright
Error: Patches for Playwright failed due to missing scoped_refptr definition. Fix: Added #include "api/scoped_refptr.h" to juggler/screencast/HeadlessWindowCapturer.h.

2. Build System & Patch Logic Fixes
I encountered a logical conflict between scripts/patch.py, copy-additions.sh, and git reset.

The Problem:

scripts/patch.py resets the repo (git reset --hard unpatched).

copy-additions.sh copies files from additions/ (overwriting current files).

Then patches are applied.

Issue: If I fix a file in additions/, the patch might fail because the context has changed (or the fix is already there). If I rely only on patches, git reset wipes my manual fixes before the build.

My Solution (The "Double Assurance" Strategy): I modified the files in additions/ to include the fixes (ensuring they exist even if patches fail) AND created a comprehensive patch file.

Crucially, I had to modify scripts/patch.py to handle "Reversed Patches" intelligently. If copy-additions.sh has already introduced the fix, the patch tool sees it as a "Reversed patch" and fails.

Modification to scripts/patch.py: I updated _apply_and_check to inspect .rej files. If the rejection is because the code (e.g., typedef int pid_t) is already present, it ignores the error and proceeds.

Python

# Logic added to scripts/patch.py to ignore harmless rejections
if 'typedef int pid_t' in rej_content and 'typedef int pid_t' in content:
    continue # Fix already exists
if 'mozilla/gfx/2D.h' in rej_content and 'mozilla/gfx/2D.h' in content:
    continue # Include already exists
3. Feature Request: Fingerprint Persistence / Reuse
Beyond the compilation issues, I have a critical requirement regarding browser fingerprinting.

Current Behavior: Camoufox seems to rotate or randomize fingerprints/canvas noise effectively for evasion.

The Need: I need a way to persist/reuse a specific fingerprint profile across sessions.

Use Case: Managing high-trust accounts where a consistent device fingerprint (Hardware concurrency, Canvas noise, Audio context, etc.) is required to avoid triggering security flags during subsequent logins.

Problem: Currently, when I restart the browser or start a new session, the fingerprint characteristics change. I attempted to implement this but faced stability issues.

Request: Could you expose an interface (via args or preferences) to:

Export the current calculated fingerprint seed/configuration.

Inject a specific fingerprint seed/configuration on startup to ensure the browser identity remains bit-exact with a previous session.

I hope this report helps improve Windows support. I am happy to submit a PR with my changes to patch.py and the header fixes if needed.

Because Camoufox performs quite complex operations internally to configure stealth-related settings in pythonlib.

For example, the `utils.py` file located in Camoufox’s `pythonlib` merges these configurations to ensure stealth-related features function properly: https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/7adc6dc17ad5692951d720a4dcdf8d6680ad6d76/pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py#L337-L662

You could run it while keeping settings and other configurations as similar as possible, but this process is quite cumbersome, so I don’t recommend it.

# Issue #473: Glyph Mapping Failure Analysis

## Bug Report Summary

**Issue**: Glyph mapping failure(?) on some websites
**Platform**: macOS Sequoia 15.6.1
**Symptoms**: Pages rendered with jumbled boxes, random symbols, and mismatched characters (mojibake)

**Affected Sites**:
- https://www.medline.com/ce/product/Rhapsody-H-30-Holmium-Laser-System/Z05-PF166789
- https://fingerprint-scan.com/
- https://bot.sannysoft.com/

## Root Cause Analysis

### Primary Cause: Accept-Encoding Header Bug

The issue is caused by an **incomplete Accept-Encoding spoofing implementation** combined with Firefox 146's new zstd compression support.

#### Bug 1: Incomplete Accept-Encoding Override

**Location**: `patches/network-patches.patch` → `nsHttpHandler.cpp`

**Current (buggy) code**:
```cpp
nsresult nsHttpHandler::SetAcceptEncodings(const char* aAcceptEncodings,
                                           bool isSecure) {
  if (auto value = MaskConfig::GetString("headers.Accept-Encoding")) {
    mHttpsAcceptEncodings.Assign(nsCString(value.value().c_str()));  // ❌ Only sets HTTPS!
    return NS_OK;  // ❌ Returns early, never sets HTTP!
  }
  if (isSecure) {
    mHttpsAcceptEncodings = aAcceptEncodings;
  } else {
    mHttpAcceptEncodings = aAcceptEncodings;
  }
  return NS_OK;
}
```

**Issues**:
1. Only sets `mHttpsAcceptEncodings`, leaves `mHttpAcceptEncodings` potentially uninitialized
2. Returns early, skipping the `isSecure` branch entirely when config is set
3. HTTP requests may use incorrect Accept-Encoding value

#### Bug 2: Missing zstd in BrowserForge Accept-Encoding

**Background**: Firefox 126+ added zstd (Zstandard) compression support:
- Old Accept-Encoding: `gzip, deflate, br`
- New Accept-Encoding: `gzip, deflate, br, zstd`

BrowserForge may generate older fingerprints without zstd. When this happens:
1. Browser sends: `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br` (no zstd)
2. CDN/server may still send zstd-compressed content (caching, misconfiguration, etc.)
3. Browser receives compressed content it "didn't ask for"
4. Content fails to decompress properly → mojibake

### Why macOS Sequoia Specifically?

While the bug affects all platforms, macOS users may notice it more because:
1. macOS Sequoia 15.6.1 is a recent release with updated CoreText/font APIs
2. CDNs may serve different content based on User-Agent (macOS gets different cached responses)
3. Web fonts are particularly affected by compression issues

## Technical Details

### How Accept-Encoding Works in Camoufox

```
User Config                 BrowserForge               Python Library
    │                            │                          │
    │  config={"headers..."}     │  generate_fingerprint()  │
    └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────
                                  ↓
                         CAMOU_CONFIG_* env vars
                                  ↓
                         MaskConfig.hpp (C++)
                                  ↓
                         nsHttpHandler.cpp
                                  ↓
                    mHttpsAcceptEncodings (ONLY!)
                                  ↓
                         HTTP/HTTPS Requests
```

### Firefox 146+ Accept-Encoding Default

Firefox 146 defaults to advertising zstd support:
```
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd
```

This is controlled by:
- `network.http.accept-encoding.secure` preference
- Built into `nsHttpHandler.cpp` initialization

### Relevant Source Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `patches/network-patches.patch` | Accept-Encoding spoofing patch |
| `netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpHandler.cpp` | HTTP handler implementation |
| `pythonlib/camoufox/browserforge.yml` | BrowserForge → Camoufox config mapping |
| `pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py` | Config processing |
| `scripts/fix-firefox146.sh` | Post-patch verification script |

## Proposed Fixes

### Fix 1: Update network-patches.patch

Set both `mHttpsAcceptEncodings` AND `mHttpAcceptEncodings`:

```cpp
nsresult nsHttpHandler::SetAcceptEncodings(const char* aAcceptEncodings,
                                           bool isSecure) {
  if (auto value = MaskConfig::GetString("headers.Accept-Encoding")) {
    nsCString encoding(value.value().c_str());
    mHttpsAcceptEncodings.Assign(encoding);
    mHttpAcceptEncodings.Assign(encoding);  // ✅ Also set HTTP encoding
    return NS_OK;
  }
  if (isSecure) {
    mHttpsAcceptEncodings = aAcceptEncodings;
  } else {
    mHttpAcceptEncodings = aAcceptEncodings;
  }
  return NS_OK;
}
```

### Fix 2: Ensure zstd in Accept-Encoding

Add to `pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py`:

```python
def ensure_zstd_encoding(config: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Ensure zstd is in Accept-Encoding for FF126+ compatibility."""
    key = 'headers.Accept-Encoding'
    if key in config:
        encoding = config[key]
        if 'zstd' not in encoding.lower():
            # Append zstd to existing encoding
            config[key] = encoding.rstrip(',') + ', zstd'
    else:
        # Set default modern Accept-Encoding
        config[key] = 'gzip, deflate, br, zstd'
```

Call this in `launch_options()` before returning config:
```python
# In launch_options(), before return:
ensure_zstd_encoding(config)
```

### Fix 3: Update fix-firefox146.sh Verification

Add verification that both encodings are set:

```python
# In scripts/fix-firefox146.sh, add check for dual assignment
verification_pattern = r'mHttpsAcceptEncodings\.Assign.*\n.*mHttpAcceptEncodings\.Assign'
```

### Fix 4: Add User Override Option (Optional)

Allow users to bypass Accept-Encoding spoofing entirely:

```python
# In config
config={
    "headers.Accept-Encoding": None  # Use Firefox default
}
```

## Testing Verification

After applying fixes, verify:

1. **Check header in browser DevTools**:
   - Open affected site
   - Network tab → Check request headers
   - `Accept-Encoding` should include `zstd`

2. **Test affected sites**:
   ```python
   import asyncio
   from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox

   async with AsyncCamoufox() as browser:
       page = await browser.new_page()
       await page.goto("https://fingerprint-scan.com/")
       # Page should render correctly without mojibake
   ```

3. **Verify both HTTP and HTTPS**:
   - Test HTTP URLs
   - Test HTTPS URLs
   - Both should use correct Accept-Encoding

## Related Issues

- Firefox zstd implementation: [Bug 1871963](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1871963)
- Firefox 126 added zstd support
- Chrome 123 added zstd support

## Alternative Theories (if Accept-Encoding fix doesn't resolve)

If the issue persists, investigate these:

1. **Font file corruption**: Web fonts (WOFF2) compressed with zstd failing to decompress
2. **macOS CoreText changes**: Sequoia 15.6.1 may have different font rendering behavior
3. **Unicode normalization**: NFD vs NFC issues with font paths (see recent commits 4e6ce89, 3776c0e)
4. **HarfBuzz glyph spacing**: The anti-font-fingerprinting patch modifies glyph positions which might interact poorly with certain fonts

## References

- [zstd Content-Encoding support table](https://caniuse.com/zstd)
- [Firefox zstd implementation bug](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1871963)
- [Accept-Encoding header MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Accept-Encoding)
- [zstd header article](https://deviceandbrowserinfo.com/learning_zone/articles/zstd-header)
